subject.title: Show DeepSeek Platform usage with cost summary

question: Should an already-saved non-Off Cost summary preference be allowed to newly authorize selected-Chrome-session DeepSeek Platform usage, or must existing users retain a separate explicit opt-in or re-consent step?
rationale: This is a persisted-setting and browser-session consent boundary; the code can implement either policy, but maintainers must choose the intended upgrade semantics before a safe repair is defined.

options.title: Preserve separate browser-session opt-in
options.body: Keep the existing credits/extras-style consent gate for DeepSeek Platform enrichment and use Cost summary only to choose how already-authorized detailed usage is displayed.

options.title: Add explicit upgrade re-consent
options.body: Allow Cost summary to govern the feature only after a one-time, visible migration or confirmation leaves existing saved preferences non-authorizing by default.

options.title: Accept implicit authorization
options.body: Treat every existing enabled Cost summary setting as consent and document that upgrade behavior explicitly.

recommendation.title: Preserve separate browser-session opt-in
recommendation.body: Keep the existing credits/extras-style consent gate for DeepSeek Platform enrichment and use Cost summary only to choose how already-authorized detailed usage is displayed.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the merged DeepSeek browser-session usage feature and authored the current gating change, making them the closest technical routing candidate for the consent-boundary decision.
